games.missing: Retail-save support is explicitly partial: bundled 409-byte character import only, plus an existing-record-preserving character codec—not arbitrary selected-folder full-save import or Greybox-session party/quest export. Continuous wilderness stepping, its visit cadence, a fresh-campaign setter for [0x4C5C], the wider landmark quest graph, CoK MIDI, exhaustive combat/rules parity, and pixel-exact coverage of every screen remain open. Round 33 (2026-09-04) resolved half of the CoK music question and turned the other half into a measured negative. The driver's CX/ES install handshake is now directly observed in live memory (two distinct nonzero segment values against an on-disk default of 0x0000). The MIDI.DAX music-timeline buffer is still not located, and now for a stated reason: both live buffers captured through that handshake decode cleanly but appear verbatim inside SOUND.DAX's SFX bank, so they are sound effects, not songs. Round 34 (2026-09-04): the ECL walker's 33 deep desync sites are now explained, not merely counted -- every one shares first byte 0x41, an opcode entirely missing from the base Gen1 table (dense only through 0x40). That override has since LANDED in the shared base table (packages/engine/src/ecl/opcodes.ts, ECL_OPCODE_MAX 0x40 -> 0x41), taking this title's deep desync count to 0 with zero shallow-census regression, and it independently agrees with Buck Rogers' own binary-derived override for the same opcode. A follow-up then read the handler itself: CoK's own GAME.OVR carries a 0x41 dispatch entry at 0x4048 whose handler reads exactly 2 operands, divides a script-supplied round amount by the count of active party members, and accumulates the share into a 32-bit per-character field, walking the party through the SAME CCH +0x17F/+0x181 "next combatant" pointer that CoK's already byte-verified post-combat calc_battle_exp uses. The mnemonic is now GEN1_AWARD_XP, still flagged uncertain because no doc here names that accumulator as the canonical experience field. R1's own "operand is always a multiple of 500" is corrected to 98.4% (121/123) with two genuine CoK exceptions (300 and 32633), against a 0.53% null over 29,954 other reached word operands. A from-cold, unscripted VM run also reaches one of these 33 sites (block 16, offset 0x79a, off the default searchLocation flow) -- a real desync a genuine playthrough could hit today, not just a census number; the round's own expectation of zero executed sites did not hold. Separately, CoK's SOUND.DAX block 1 -- previously measured as an SFX bank, not the missing music buffer -- turns out to hold real song-shaped content too: three long, balanced, multi-voice passages (up to 5,132 events, 5 voices, near-perfect Note-On/Off balance), one of which the resident AdLib driver's own live cursor sits inside during both a splash screen and demo gameplay (three independent RAM captures, no new DOSBox-X session). This is still not a hardware-output proof -- no OUT to port 0x388 was traced this round -- and the decoder is not yet wired into the app's audio path. Round 35 R2 (2026-09-05) corrects the event-framing numbers just above: the event record is THREE bytes, not one (2 data bytes + 1 trailing wait byte for note events; measured from the driver's own code, not assumed). The three song-like SOUND.DAX passages are 1,601 / 381 / 1,712 events each -- not "up to 5,132" -- 3,699 real events in total (3,700 with the decoder's own terminal-marker count), across 7 segments, not 14; Note-On/Note-Off pairs are 1,846/1,846 against a shuffled-column null of 0.540. The directional finding (this buffer holds song-shaped content, not merely SFX) is unchanged; only the counts moved. It is still decode-only, and the decoder is still not wired into the app's audio path. docs/engine/research/cok-sound-bank-framing.md.

Round 34 (2026-09-04): the same missing opcode 0x41 explains 47 of DoK's 72 deep ECL desync sites (byte shape 41 00 [01] 0[23] <round-number word>, consistent with a reward/XP award, unconfirmed); a test-local override reduces the count to 29, not to zero -- DoK's residual sites are scattered across roughly 20 further first bytes, a real, unclosed dialect gap rather than one more single opcode. A from-cold, unscripted VM run also reaches one DIFFERENT DoK site (block 33, offset 0x51b, first byte 0x80), only 5 instructions past a straightforward branch. The opcode-table fix has since LANDED in the shared base table and this title's ledger count moved with it, 72 -> 29 (the residual 29 remain a separate, unclosed dialect gap and are not attributed to 0x41). DoK's own GAME.OVR carries a 0x41 dispatch entry at 0x2e0e -- reproducing the pre-existing build/dok-ecl-dispatch-map.json row byte-for-byte -- whose handler reads exactly 2 operands and implements the same divide-among-active-party-members accumulate as CoK's, so the opcode is now GEN1_AWARD_XP rather than UNKNOWN_0x41, still flagged uncertain. DoK's handler additionally calls out once more right after the accumulate, storing the returned byte into the character record; that call was not identified. Round 35 R1 (2026-09-05) CORRECTS THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE: there was no second, separate opcode gap. DoK's residual 29 deep-desync sites were an artifact of running DoK's own ECL under the SHARED ECL_GEN1_SHORT dialect. DoK has its own distinct dialect, ECL_GEN1_SHORT_DOK, which round 34 had already decoded but left unwired -- solved but unreachable, since no app code imported it. The dialect itself, exercised directly by packages/engine/test/eclReachability.test.ts, closes the deep-desync residual to 0 across all 25 retail ECL1-3.DAX blocks (misaligned targets 202 -> 2, reachable bytes 132,423 -> 140,730). Under DoK's own dialect the pre-0x41 reconstruction is 58 of 58 sites first-byte 0x41 (100%, up from 47 of 72 = 65% under the shared dialect), so DoK joins CoK and Secret as a corpus 0x41 fully explains. The block-33/offset-0x51b/first-byte-0x80 site the from-cold VM run reached is also closed by this same fix -- it was DoK's own operand-count drift under the wrong dialect, not a second gap. docs/engine/research/dok-ecl-word-sets.md, packages/engine/test/eclReachability.test.ts. STILL SOLVED BUT UNWIRED AT THE APP LEVEL as of this measurement: packages/engine/src/index.ts does not re-export ECL_GEN1_SHORT_DOK, and apps/web/src/ui/explore.ts (openDokTravel, the DoK overland dialogue call, and both DoK VM constructions), apps/web/src/ui/gen1Profiles.ts's DOK_DEMO_PROFILE, and tools/build-dqk-dir.mts still construct DoK's ECL VM under the SHARED ECL_GEN1_SHORT dialect, not its own. No gameplay route has exercised the 0-residual reading yet.

games.web_text: The retail DOS install is read: 73 DAX containers, 570 members, 0 parse failures on the existing Gen1 reader, and a deep binary map of its GAME.OVR. Its overlay magic is TPOV, not the FBOV the other Gen1 titles carry — only Secret of the Silver Blades shares that. Since 2026-08-26 it also has a browser asset manifest in the game picker, rendering 489 frames across its title, scene, portrait, tile, sprite and UI families. That is an asset preview, not a playability claim: no browser route mounts the game.
games.asm_text: Deep binary map present: TPOV overlay, 34 descriptors, 23 anchors, 41 selector rows, 8 resolved.
games.missing: No declared retail route, so no leg of the campaign matrix is exercised. Buck's ECL dialect HAS now been verified against its own binary (ECL_GEN1_BUCK, derived from GAME.OVR's own dispatcher and operand prefetches; 23 of its 25 retail blocks disassemble to a clean EXIT and 2 still desync (ecl1.dax#18@0x395, ecl6.dax#99@0x2c0, both genuinely unattributed); round 30 attempted to close what was then 4 desyncs, calibrated a linear segment-to-file-offset mapping on Curse of the Azure Bonds where an oracle names every call target, fit only 9 of 103 calls against its own 10-call bar, and landed the negative rather than an uncalibrated address; round 31 narrowed that negative (a non-linear stub-geometry resolver reached 3 of the 7 blocking call targets, calibrated on the same oracle at 229 of 240 targets) but the desync count still did not move, since every resolved chain bottomed out in unread, still-EXEPACK-compressed resident code; round 32 retracts the rest of that negative outright rather than narrowing it again — a new unpacker confirmed Buck's GAME.OVR loader is genuine Microsoft EXEPACK v1, and against the unpacked resident image the same CoAB-oracle check that read 0 of 140 Borland-prologue landings against packed bytes reads 66 of 140 (47%) at shift 0 versus 0 of 140 at +/-1; walking the three opcodes' full resident call graphs to exhaustion shows none ever touches the ECL PC global or calls the operand parser, so 0x29 ENCOUNTER_MENU, 0x2c PARLAY and 0x42 all now read as wordSet 0 off Buck's own binary, closing 2 of the then-4 remaining desyncs), and round 29 gave Buck the capability ledger's twelfth profile — but its XXVc rules contracts are still unbuilt and no gameplay route executes Buck ECL against live game state. Round 33 (2026-09-04) moved two of this title's rows and left the biggest one where it was. MUSIC.DAX is now decoded rather than merely catalogued -- 8 GLBR songs, 1959 events, 31 channel streams, censused by loadGame and shown in the dashboard header -- but that is a decode result, not playback: a byte scan of this title's own driver blob finds no AdLib or CMS port immediate anywhere, so nothing shows it reaching sound hardware. The GEO, WALLDEF and ECL containers are confirmed to decode with the same Gen1 loaders already proven on CoK/DoK (17 GEO blocks at 1026 bytes, 9 WALLDEF each a multiple of 780, 25 ECL all carrying the 0x1388 magic, 16 paired GEO/ECL areas across the six C64 sides), which corrects a ledger entry that had called them un-reverse-engineered. Monster and item records genuinely are not: 263-byte monster records and a 1456-byte item table match no existing layout profile, contradicting the round's own prediction. And the clean-EXIT count quoted above is a LOWER BOUND -- an all-entry-point walk of the same 25 blocks finds 195 deep desync sites, because the shallow scan stops at each block's first EXIT. Round 34 (2026-09-04): the 259/263-byte monster-record puzzle round 33 flagged is now a shared XXVc record family, not two orphan sizes. Buck's own six chrdata{n}.sav pregens (259 bytes, uncompressed, no DAX wrapper) decode name/abilities/HP/morale, and the same layout explains Matrix Cubed's own 259-byte monster records; Buck's own 263-byte monster record is that layout with 4 bytes inserted near offset 251 (located by a per-offset crossover analysis, after the plan's own shuffled-pairing null failed to reproduce -- VOID as stated). AC, THAC0, damage, category, hit dice and XP were NOT located -- no lookup routine was found in GAME.OVR or START.EXE and no monster-manual table is digitized here -- so no seventh MonsterLayoutProfile was added, deliberately avoiding a fit to the nearest size. Round 35 (2026-09-05) corrected the sentence that stood here: it said 'the new decoder is not yet wired into the engine's index.ts or any import UI', which the very next commit falsified. The decoder is exported from the engine's index.ts and is shown by the ?import=buck panel -- but display-only: it never calls createCharacter, because no race, class or level byte has been located in the record, so nothing it decodes reaches the rules layer or a playable party. Two more corrections, both self-contradiction fixes rather than new bytes: the ledger's own gaps bullet still denying GEO/WALLDEF were reverse-engineered (they already were, per the same entry's own detail) has been narrowed to the families still genuinely unmapped (monster, item); and this title's GLBR music claim is corrected from 'a SIX-title format' to 'a FIVE-title format' -- Matrix Cubed's identically-named MUSIC.DAX turned out to be an unopened leftover copy, not a second confirmation. Round 35 R1 (2026-09-05) corrects the desync count named early in this entry: opcode 0x42 was inert through round 34 -- a bare wordSetOverrides key with no matching opcodeOverrides definition, so byte 0x42 still decoded as a bad opcode. Moving it into a real opcodeOverrides entry this round closes ecl1.dax#18@0x395 (it sat on that opcode), leaving 24 of 25 retail blocks clean and ONE residual desync, not two: ecl6.dax#99@0x2c0. No semantics beyond operand width are claimed for 0x42. docs/engine/research/buck-matrix-opcode-42.md.

games.missing: Round 30 extracted the DOS release into git-ignored matrixcubed_extracted/ (the source .7z on the external drive stays read-only and nothing auto-extracts), landed a browser manifest and the capability ledger's thirteenth profile, and corrected the detection profile's display claim to dos-vga against bytes. Round 31 closed the ECL gap this entry used to name: a dispatch map was built from Matrix Cubed's OWN GAME.OVR - whose overlay magic is FBOV, Curse of the Azure Bonds' magic, not Countdown's TPOV, so nothing was assumed to transfer - and shipped as ECL_GEN1_MATRIX behind the ?ecl=matrix inspector. Round 32 unpacked Matrix's own EXEPACK-compressed GAME.OVR resident image and walked 0x29 ENCOUNTER_MENU/0x2c PARLAY/0x42's full call graphs to exhaustion, finding none of them ever touches the ECL PC global or calls the operand parser - resolving all three to wordSet 0 independently of Buck's binary. 30 of the 33 retail ECL blocks now reach a clean terminating EXIT and 3 desync (was 29/4): one site (block 1) is fully resolved, one (block 18) trades its old masked stop for a new downstream one the fix reveals rather than closes, and two (blocks 20, 24) are unrelated and unchanged.
